strategiesExperience using AI-powered tools to enhance content development and marketing efficiencyInsight into how sales and marketing teams collaborate to drive business growthOpportunities to work jobs.description: Employer: Qualcomm - Engineering Expires: 10/19/2026 About QualcommQualcomm relentlessly innovates transforming businesses, enriching lives and fortifying societies. Our solutions are pivotal in crafting a smarter, interconnected world. Building on our nearly 40-year history of era-defining technology breakthroughs, we deliver leading-edge AI, high performance, lower-power computing, and unrivaled connectivity. We’re proud to be the partner of choice to many of the world’s largest enterprises. Together with our ecosystem partners, we enable next-generation digital transformation. At Qualcomm, we are engineering human progress.Join Us in Shaping the FutureAt Qualcomm, we're committed to engineering human progress by delivering intelligent computing everywhere. We're passionate about harnessing the power of technology to transform industries and improve lives. Our early career programs offer limitless opportunities for growth, mentorship, and meaningful work. By joining our team, you'll be part of a community that's pushing the boundaries of what's possible in AI, computing, and connectivity. With a global footprint spanning over 30 countries, you'll have the chance to collaborate with diverse talent and contribute to projects that are shaping the future of technology.Our early career programs are designed to attract inventive minds, offering a platform to contribute to our long-term innovation pipeline. You'll be part of a community that values collaboration, creativity, and continuous learning. Our programs provide real-world experience, technical skills, and professional development opportunities, empowering you to make a meaningful impact and achieve your career goals. Join us for our U.S. 2027 summer intern class!Maximize Your Opportunities:Our internship hiring model routes candidates from this application into multiple project specific roles. Your "Profile Visibility" choice will guide how we manage your data across our systems. To be considered for the full breadth of internship opportunities, select the option to use your profile data for "Any Roles Globally". If you choose to limit your data to "Only The Role I'm Applying For", it will restrict the opportunity for you to be considered across matching internship opportunities. You can update your profile visibility preferences at any time through the Candidate Home Portal. Steps:Log Into Your Eightfold Candidate Home Account Hover Over The "Profile" Dropdown Open Settings Edit "Profile Visibility" Role OverviewAs a Qualcomm Product Management intern, you will assist in business operations by gathering and analyzing data, generating reports, and presenting findings to senior management. Support in business development and partnerships across the ecosystem, using strong verbal and written communication skills to convey complex information to diverse audiences. Additionally, you will review customer requirements, identify gaps in Qualcomm’s offerings, and exercise creativity and problem-solving skills to innovate and suggest new products or processes, often dealing with incomplete or conflicting information.This internship supports the Product Management track. Based on your resume, you will be aligned to projects within this track.Minimum QualificationsCurrently enrolled in a bachelor’s, master’s, or Ph.D. degree program in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Business, or a related field.Must be available for 11–14 weeks during Summer 2027 (May–September).Expected graduation date of November 2027 or later.1+ years of academic or project experience in:Product marketing and data analysisRequirement gathering and interpretationData engineering and analyticsTools such as Excel, Pivot Tables, PowerPoint, and data modelingPreferred QualificationsCandidates actively pursuing a degree with an anticipated graduation between November 2027 and June 2028 Currently enrolled in a Master’s or MBA program in Computer Engineering, Business, or a related field.Completed a bachelor’s degree or minor in Electrical Engineering or Computer EngineeringAcademic or project experience in: Product marketing, silicon technology, computer processing, and AI processing2+ years of experience in a technical roleProgramming experience in C++, Python, C, or JavaQualcomm’s Internship ProgramOur interns join world-class teams to help define and build what is next for mobility and the world. You’ll be paired with a mentor with visibility to your project and team, receive support from your manager, and have access to the entire Qualcomm employee community to ensure your success. To round out your summer internship, we host professional development workshops, social events, cross-functional speaker sessions, and an executive speaker series. In addition to competitive hourly pay and accrued vacation time, you will receive relocation coverage and furnished housing accommodations for the duration of your internship.Internship opportunities may be available in the following locations, depending on team and project needs: Austin, Boulder, Boxborough, Bridgewater, Chandler, Irvine, New York City, Louisville, Raleigh, San Diego, Santa Clara, and Seattle.Application ProcessBy applying here, you are expressing interest in one of our many 2027 Qualcomm Product Management internships. It is important to note that this is not a job posting for a specific project. We will review resumes on an ongoing basis, and a recruiter may reach out to you.Future Employment ConsiderationsThis internship aligns to a potential role that is not eligible for Qualcomm immigration sponsorship.Export Control NoticeThis role may require an export license for candidates with citizenship in certain countries (see current country list below – subject to change). (Keep in mind that this email address is used to provide reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities. jobs.title: Nonprofit Accelerator Internship at University Impact
jobs.description: Employer: University Impact Expires: 10/21/2026 Nonprofit Accelerator Internship – UI Charitable Outcomes Lab(Priority Applications Due 9.25.2026) BackgroundUI Charitable helps financial advisors and their clients give more impactfully. We work with ~1,300 families and ~400 financial advisors, and we manage $500+ million in charitable assets. More importantly, we have moved over $350 million out the door to nonprofits and impact investments working to improve the world's most pressing social and environmental issues. Why We Think This Work Matters NowTwo forces are about to reshape philanthropy. The AI boom is creating a new generation of wealth, and the founders and employees holding that ownership are deciding how to structure their giving. Most of them will want to move money out faster than the sector can absorb it. Over the same period, as much as $124 trillion will change hands through 2048, with an anticipated $18 trillion of it going to charity. We are building the infrastructure to turn that money into real improvements in people's lives. The Problem You Will Work on For This InternshipA lot of charitable dollars do not produce the lasting change donors expect. Plenty of funded organizations will never solve the problem they exist to solve, and money alone will not fix that. Most attempts to address this try to change donor behavior, including several of our own. So we are working on the organizations instead. What We Are BuildingEight years of building the infrastructure gives us a direct relationship with thousands of nonprofits our donors already fund. We want to help them become more effective. The closest analogy is a business accelerator for nonprofits, or a private equity operating team. We assess an organization across the core functions of a well-run business, run it through a cohort based program, and reassess later to see what moved. So far we have a literature review, a survey of 150 nonprofits, an analysis of our own data, and some first drafts of our curriculum and a way we will measure the success of the program. We will judge the program by whether those organizations actually improve, not by how many attend. The Eight Functions We want all organizations our donors give to, to have a sound understanding of their outcomes and impact. But in order to do that, you have to be running an effective/efficient organization. We are organizing the program around the functions that separate organizations that grow from organizations that stall. Each intern will own work across multiple of these functions.Fundraising and the growth engine. Treating donor development as a sales pipeline with stages, conversion rates, and follow-up. (Sales, Marketing, and Branding)AI adoption and operations. Where AI can take real work off a five-person staff. Marketing and branding. Making the case for support to people who have never heard of the organization.Board development and governance. What effective boards do, and how to get a board to do it.Program measurement and evaluation. Outputs, outcomes, and impact, and how small organizations can measure honestly without a research budget. (Public Health, Statistics, etc.)Finance, accounting, and internal controls. Who approves spending, who reconciles accounts, and what gets outsourced.Technology and data systems. CRM, donor records, and reporting that does not live in the executive director’s head.Talent and leadership capacity. Hiring, retention, and how a small team allocates the hours it has. Position OverviewWe are hiring two interns to help run a year-long pilot. You will work directly with Gary McHardy (a Rhodes Scholar based in South Africa) and Tanner Mills (Sr. Associate at UI Charitable). The team is small and the program is new, which means you will own real pieces of the work rather than support someone else’s. Segment organizations by size, growth trend, and reported need using assessment results and public financials.Measure our own results and make adjustments. jobs.title: Marketing & Growth Lead at Forbidden Well
jobs.description: Employer: Forbidden Well Expires: 10/22/2026 Marketing & Growth Lead (Paid Internship → Full-Time)Forbidden Well · New York, NY · Hybrid, 2 days a week on site$1,500/month · 90-day paid internship, designed to convert to full-time This is a six-figure job on the other side of 90 days.The internship pays $1,500/month. The full-time role it converts into starts at $75,000 and can exceed $150,000 based on performance and the revenue you generate. We built the path that way on purpose — we'd rather pay it out than not. You will own marketing. All of it.This is not an internship where you're handed a task list and asked to schedule someone else's posts. You will own the strategy, the calendar, the campaigns and the creative. The concepts are yours. The pitch ideas are yours. The call on what we run next is yours.We'll work alongside you to stay aligned on direction and make sure you have what you need, but you are not waiting on us to tell you what to do. If you need someone to hand you assignments, this is the wrong job. If you've been waiting for someone to hand you the keys instead, read on. You are the keeper of the brandForbidden Well should look and sound like one thing everywhere we show up: email campaigns, social posts, stories, the grid, and every other form of communication we put out. Someone should be able to see any piece of our content and know instantly that it's us.That means more than staying consistent. You'll continuously fine-tune that identity, stay organized in how we market, and be deliberate about what goes out and why. No random posting. Every piece has a purpose you can explain.You own every external relationshipThis role owns all points of contact with other spas, vendors, modeling agencies and brands — curating them, organizing them, and keeping them alive over time.A real example: a friend recently connected us to the owner of a very successful spa in Miami. We make the introduction, and from there it's yours to develop into something lucrative — a referral partnership where their clients coming to New York come to us, and ours heading to Miami go to them. First introduction to signed, working partnership, end to end. That's the job. What you'll runBrand, content and social across Instagram and TikTok: your concepts, your voice, your calendarBrand consistency across every channel we touch, and the standards that keep it that wayEmail marketing, including weekly campaigns and automated flowsPaid social and lead generation campaigns with our agency partnerPartnerships and outreach: spas, vendors, modeling agencies and like-minded brands, plus the co-marketing campaigns that come out of themPhoto and video shoots: concept, casting, scheduling and running the dayOur podcast, using our full in-house studio: booking guests, recording, editing and publishingLocal search, our Google Business Profile and our Google reviews programDaily and weekly reporting on what's working Who this is forYou generate ideas without being asked and can defend themYou write well and have taste. You can tell the difference between good and almost goodYou have an eye for consistency and it bothers you when something is off-brandYou're comfortable talking to people and turning an introduction into a relationship that lastsYou're comfortable with AI tools, especially Claude, and use them to move fasterYou're organized enough to run a shoot, a podcast taping and three campaigns in the same weekYou want to build something, not pad a resume Where it goesThis 90-day period is a prerequisite for a full-time, long-term role, and it's how we both find out if this is the right fit. We're hiring for the person who runs marketing at Forbidden Well for years — someone who grows as the company does and takes on more as we open more. If you hit the benchmarks, which we'll set with you and review together, the full-time role starts at $75,000 and can exceed $150,000 based on performance and revenue generated. About usForbidden Well is a luxury wellness house in New York built around IV therapy, advanced treatments and a client experience that feels like nothing else in the city.Apply with your resume and anything you've made that you're proud of: content, campaigns, a brand you built, a project that worked. Tell us about one brand whose identity you think is airtight and why, and one relationship or partnership you started and kept going. We care more about what you've shipped than where you've interned.

jobs.description: Employer: Graco Inc. Expires: 10/22/2026 The purpose of this position is to provide immersive, strategic-level experience within Graco’s Category Marketing team. At Graco, Category Marketing focuses on understanding and growing specific customer segments and industries (often referred to as market verticals), helping the business identify opportunities, understand customer needs, and shape strategies that drive growth. In this role, the intern will lead a defined strategic project for an assigned customer segment under the mentorship of the Director of Category Marketing. The intern will leverage market research, Voice of Customer (VOC) insights, competitive analysis, and go-to-market strategy to address a real business challenge. The experience culminates in the development and presentation of a strategic recommendation to Graco’s Executive Leadership Team. This internship is designed for MBA candidates seeking a long-term career in category marketing, product marketing, strategic marketing, or general management. Program Structure: This summer internship is centered on a high-value strategic project that addresses a real business opportunity or challenge within an assigned category and which has the potential to shape future growth initiatives. The project is supplemented by exposure to the broader category marketing function and close collaboration with cross-functional partners, including product management, channel marketing, corporate marketing, and sales. The internship culminates in a strategic recommendation presented to senior internship. What You Will Do at Graco Strategic Project Experience Lead a high-impact strategic project focused on a real business opportunity or challenge within an assigned customer segment or industry. Work closely with a Category Marketing leader to define the project scope, conduct analysis, and develop recommendations. Apply market research, customer insights, and business strategy concepts to address a meaningful business question. Develop and present a final recommendation to senior leaders at the conclusion of the internship. Market and Customer Insights Conduct market, customer, and competitive research to better understand industry trends and customer needs. Analyze Voice of Customer (VOC) feedback and other data sources to identify key insights and opportunities. Learn how customer and market insights are used to shape busness and marketing strategies. Cross-Functional Collaboration Collaborate with teams across product management, sales, channel marketing, and corporate marketing Gain exposure to how strategy is developed and translated into product launches, marketing campaigns, and commercial execution. Coordinate with internal subject matter experts to validate research findings and assumptions. Participate in team meetings, project reviews, and business discussions to better understand Graco's growth strategy. Professional Development Build skills in strategic thinking, business analysis, executive communication, and problem solving. Receive coaching and mentorship from experienced marketing leaders throughout the internship. Develop and deliver a professional executive-level presentation summarizing project findings and recommendations. Other duties and learning opportunities as assigned. What You Will Bring to Graco Currently pursuing an MBA, with an expected graduation date within 12–18 months of the internship Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business Administration, or a related field Prior experience in marketing, business strategy, or vertical-specific market development (internship or professional) preferred Team collaborator with experience working in multi-functional or global team settings Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret and synthesize VOC insights and market research into clear recommendations Excellent communication and presentation skills, including comfort presenting to senior leadership Ability to manage ambiguity and drive a project forward with limited day-to-day direction

Innovation & Improvement:Contribute creative ideas to enhance campaign engagement and improve client satisfaction.Stay updated on trends in digital design, benefits communication, and workforce development for continuous improvement.Help establish standard operating procedures (SOPs) to optimize process workflows in the Content department. Skills and QualificationsExperience: 1-3 years in digital content creation, graphic design, or video production, preferably in a healthcare, health benefits, or educational setting.Technical & Design Proficiency: Skilled in PowerPoint design, Adobe Creative Suite (Illustrator, Photoshop, Premiere Pro) or Canva, with basic video editing and animation experience preferred. Health Benefits Literacy & Communication: Ability to translate complex health benefits information into accessible, easy-to-understand materials. jobs.title: Sales Development Representative (SDR) — Paid Sales Internship at Andy Eaton State Farm
jobs.description: Employer: Andy Eaton State Farm Expires: 10/24/2026 The OpportunityWant to graduate with real sales experience already on your résumé?Andy Eaton State Farm is looking for a motivated college student to join our Lakewood office as a part-time Sales Development Representative (SDR). You'll receive hands-on training and build measurable experience in prospecting, lead qualification, professional communication, CRM systems, and sales performance—all while earning a guaranteed hourly wage plus performance incentives.We'll provide the leads, training, scripts, and systems. Your job is to move fast, make contact, start conversations, and create opportunities for our sales team.You won't be responsible for closing the insurance sale. Your primary objective is simple: connect with prospective customers and transfer interested, qualified prospects to our sales team.What You'll GainThis isn't just a part-time job. It's an opportunity to develop skills that translate directly into a career in sales and business.You'll gain hands-on experience in:Sales developmentProspecting and lead managementProfessional communicationOvercoming objectionsBuilding rapportWorking within a sales pipelineGoal setting and performance trackingInsurance and financial servicesFor students interested in sales, business, marketing, finance, communications, entrepreneurship, or financial services, this is an opportunity to start building your résumé while you're still in school.What You'll DoAs an SDR, you'll be on the front end of our sales process.Your responsibilities will include:Making high-volume outbound calls to leads provided by our officeWorking toward a goal of approximately 60–70 outbound calls per hourStarting friendly, professional conversations with prospective customersIdentifying prospects who are interested and available to speak with our sales teamWarm-transferring qualifying prospects directly to a sales team memberFollowing our scripts, systems, and lead follow-up processAccurately tracking calls, contacts, and transfersWorking toward individual activity and performance goalsNo cold prospecting or finding your own leads—we provide the leads for you.Who We're Looking ForWe're more interested in your drive than your résumé.You don't need previous insurance experience. You don't even need previous sales experience.We're looking for someone who is:Competitive – You like having a number to beat.Driven – You don't need someone constantly pushing you.Resilient – Rejection and unanswered calls don't slow you down.Fast-paced – You enjoy staying busy and moving quickly.Personable – You can make people comfortable and communicate naturally.Coachable – You're willing to learn, follow a process, and improve.Dependable – When you're scheduled to work, you're ready to perform.Goal-oriented – You like seeing measurable results from your effort.If you're ambitious and willing to work, we'll teach you the rest.CompensationWe believe strong performance should be rewarded.This position combines a guaranteed hourly wage with uncapped performance incentives.Base Pay: $15.16/hourPerformance Incentive: $12 for each qualifying successful lead transferThe better you perform, the more you can earn.Example Earnings0 qualifying transfers/hour: $15.16/hour1 qualifying transfer/hour: $27.16/hour2 qualifying transfers/hour: $39.16/hour3 qualifying transfers/hour: $51.16/hourThere is no predetermined cap on qualifying transfer incentives. Actual earnings will vary based on individual performance.A qualifying successful transfer occurs when you connect an eligible prospective customer with an available member of our sales team in accordance with our lead-transfer procedures. Complete qualification requirements will be provided during training and in our written incentive compensation policy.ScheduleApproximately 20 hours per weekPart-time positionIn-person at our Lakewood, Colorado officeScheduling flexibility may be available around college classes and other commitmentsSpecific working hours will be discussed during the interview processPotential Career PathFor high-performing team members who are interested in continuing in the insurance industry, this role may also provide a pathway toward becoming a licensed insurance professional and pursuing additional sales opportunities within our agency. No insurance experience or license is required to start. We'll teach you the SDR role first and give you an opportunity to demonstrate what you can do. For students interested in sales, business, marketing, finance, communications, entrepreneurship, insurance, or financial services, this is an opportunity to start building meaningful professional experience while you're still in school.Where This Could LeadStrong performance in the SDR role may open opportunities for additional responsibilities within our agency. For interns interested in building a career in insurance and financial services, there may also be a pathway toward becoming a licensed insurance professional and moving into a larger sales role.Think You Can Do It?This is a high-activity sales development role.If making 60–70 calls per hour sounds intimidating, this probably isn't the position for you.But if you're competitive, enjoy a challenge, and like the idea of earning more when you produce more, we'd like to meet you.Previous sales experience isn't required.Drive is.Apply today and tell us why you'd be a great addition to our team.

NES is for clients who do not want traditional PR. We offer a bespoke, story-driven model built on trust, editorial insight, and meaningful storytelling.

From TikTok ads and CMS updates to trip launches and organizing swag for teams. you’ll have the opportunity to work on a wide range of projects that directly influence how travelers discover and experience our brand.Consider this a professional outlet for your travel obsession.This is a cross-functional role built for someone who’s organized, curious, people-oriented, and genuinely excited about how content works across channels, across teams, and across formats. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys variety and is excited to jump between hands-on tasks—from making site updates and creating graphics to QAing content and supporting day-to-day marketing projects.You’ll partner with our Growth and Creative teams to bring content to life: building landing pages, making updates in our CMS, creating and optimizing digital ads, and ensuring our brand shows up as its best across channels. You don’t need to be an expert in all of it on day one, but you do need the drive to learn fast and the people skills to work across teams. What you’ll do -Source, organize, and create content in our CMS for the Ultimate Break website, ranging from promotional graphics to content-rich landing pages and itinerary pages -Create compelling content for paid media advertising and work with the team to optimize and refine ads for stronger performance -Support content calendars, asset libraries, and documentation for your projects so nothing falls through the cracks -Leverage agentic tools to automate repetitive production tasks: generating copy variations for landing pages, adapting email content for different segments, etc.What we’re looking for Required -Some experience in content creation and comfort with learning new systems -A keen eye for design and copy to ensure consistency of our branded content across channels -A natural communicator who’s comfortable working with different teams -A hands-on comfort with AI tools; you’ve used AI agents to get work done faster, without losing sight of taste, originality, and craft. -Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail -Strong verbal and visual communication skills with the ability to interpret direction -An interest in keeping up with (and sharing!) evolving Gen Z and Millennial trendsAdditional helpful (but not mandatory) skills: Experience working with a CMS and ad platforms -Experience working with an ecommerce/DTC brand -Some knowledge of Figma and Canva -Light video, animation, or motion skillsWhy this role You’ll get visibility across nearly every marketing function: ecommerce, paid media, CRM, and branded content. We’re a team that moves fast, values good ideas and is actively investing in how AI agents can power our workflows. The practical stuff—and why it’s part of the fun• $25 per hour: This is a paid, hourly internship.• 20–40 hours per week: We’re open to interns who can contribute anywhere from 20 to 40 hours each week. Whether you’re a student with 20 hours available or a recent graduate looking for full-time hours, we’ll work together to find a schedule that fits.• On-site collaboration: During your working hours, you’ll work from the office alongside our creative and marketing teams. We believe the best ideas often come from being in the room together—sharing feedback, brainstorming, and learning from one another. About UsSome companies are in the business of banking. Others are in the business of shoes. Or sports. Or soft drinks. At EF, we're in a different kind of business. One that's a little less tangible, and a lot more important. Because our business, what we make, makes everything else possible. We're in the business of understanding. Between people. Between cultures.For over half a century we’ve been the leader in international educational programs and experiences designed to foster such understanding. Through language, cultural exchange, academic studies, and educational travel, we create the kinds of immersive experiences that challenge biases, open minds, and pave the way for a more understanding world. You’ll find our offices and schools located in some of the world’s greatest cities, and filled with smart, driven people (over 50,000 of us) who push each other to be better every day. But it’s what we do together - building greater understanding, breaking down barriers, and creating a better world - that makes all the difference. Founded in 1965 in Sweden, EF (Education First) is a global association of education companies that share a common mission of opening the world through education. EF has been recognized on Forbes 2025 and 2024 World’s Best Employers and 2024 Top Companies for Women lists, Fast Company’s 2025 Next Big Things In Tech, and was a 2024 App Store Award winner in Cultural Impact. About the TeamAt EF Ultimate Break, we’re about way more than collecting passport stamps. Our guided tours empower young adults aged 18–35 to explore a world outside their comfort zones. Each immersive tour creates experiences that last a lifetime, building bonds with fellow travelers that go beyond borders and cultures, and help bring the world a little bit closer. WARNING: Working at Ultimate Break may inspire your own desire to experience the world, good news is- we’ll help with that! Learn more about EF Ultimate Break: https://www.efultimatebreak.com/

jobs.description: Employer: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum Expires: 10/29/2026 Internship: Creative (Paid)For application deadlines and internship dates, please visit: Countrymusichalloffame.org/support/get- involved/internships.Museum Overview: Accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum has been called the “Smithsonian of country music,” celebrated for its broad cultural impact, educational mission, and unrivaled collection of historically important artifacts. Chartered by the state of Tennessee in 1964, the Museum is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, educational organization that documents and interprets the history of country music. The Museum collects objects and archival materials that illustrate the evolving history and traditions of country music and provides diverse learning opportunities through educational programs, publications, and exhibitions.First opened in 1967 on Nashville’s Music Row, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum launched its current downtown location in 2001. In 2014, the Museum unveiled a $100 million expansion that doubled its footprint. The Museum now encompasses 350,000 square feet of exhibition galleries, archival storage, retail stores, and event space. The Museum owns Hatch Show Print, a letterpress print shop opened in 1879, and it operates Historic RCA Studio B, where Dolly Parton, Elvis Presley, and many others recorded. In addition, the Museum offers the Taylor Swift Education Center for students, teachers, and families, and dedicated performance spaces in the CMA Theater and Ford Theater, both of which regularly host nationally recognized live music and cultural events.In 2024, the Museum was awarded the prestigious National Medal of Arts by President Joe Biden. The medal is the highest award given to artists and arts institutions by the United States government. The White House Citation, which accompanied the medal, recognized the Museum’s work, which “preserves history, honors giants of the genre, and inspires future generations to write their own songs about the American story.”Internship Program Overview: The Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum offers paid internships to full-time college students (undergraduate and graduate) that advance the educational goals of the intern and help to promote the Museum’s mission. The Museum’s internship program offers work-based learning opportunities that introduce college students to museum-related careers and other professions found in large cultural organizations. Internships are designed for a maximum commitment of 25 hours per week for 12 weeks with consideration given to individual university requirements. Additional adjustments to the 12-week, 25-hour schedule will be at the discretion of the internship supervisor. Educational programs which operate on a quarterly basis may be accommodated. Motivated students who are seeking hands-on experiences in a team- oriented environment will find excellent opportunities at the Museum.The application process for prospective interns includes the submission of:An online application for the specific internship you are applying for via our internal hiring systemA resumeA one-page cover letter; it is recommended that your cover letter explain how your education and experience will contribute positively to this internship and how this internship relates to your academic pursuits and/or career goals What We Offer Interns:The hourly rate for this position is $15/hr. for students pursuing a bachelor's degree; $18/hr. for students pursuing a master's degree or higherFree 24/7 downtown parking or WeGo bus passComplimentary admission to the Museum for yourselfTwo complimentary Museum admission passes for friends and family useFree guided tour of Hatch Show Print, Historic RCA Studio B, and the Museum’s galleriesDiscounts at Museum stores and restaurantsFree or discounted entry to local venues including: National Museum of African American Music, the Opry, Ryman Auditorium, and more!Fun, friendly, and supportive learning environment Field Forward Stipend: Field Forward is a living and relocation stipend, offered to select candidates in addition to the paid internship, that supports students who identify as traditionally underrepresented in cultural arts careers and students with demonstrated financial need. Field Forward’s goals are to encourage diverse student engagement with the Museum and the broader museum field and to promote educational and professional experience and training to students historically underrepresented in museum and other cultural arts professions. Students must submit an additional application and demonstrate financial need (if applicable) to be considered. To learn more, including important deadlines, please visit: Countrymusichalloffame.org/support/get-involved/internships.Departmental Overview: The Creative department is responsible for the design and production of all exhibits, advertisements, collateral support materials, web graphics (social media, website, and email) and on- property signage – from concept to delivery. Our overall goal is to perpetuate the mission of the Museum. The Creative department interacts with nearly all other departments such as Education, Programming, Events, Development, Retail, Ticketed events, and Dining.Creative Internship Overview: The goal of this internship is to engage the intern in various areas of graphic design at the Museum including print, digital, content, project management, and vendor relationships. The intern will also learn about best practices for graphic design and how the Creative department interacts and collaborates with other Museum departments.Specific Internship Duties Include:Collaborate with Graphic Designers to create digital and print advertisements, social media graphics, on-property signage, and various collateral materials to support operations across all Museum departmentsDaily utilization of Basecamp, a project management tool, to collect job details, upload designs, gather feedback, post edits, and progress towards delivering finalized productsCoordinating projects with the Creative Department’s Project Manager and Graphic DesignersDevelop a comprehensive understanding of the institution and of the Museum’s mission RequirementsMinimum Requirements:Currently enrolled, credit-seeking, and/or degree-seeking undergraduate or graduate student pursuing a degree in graphic design, or a related fieldPreferred Requirements:Previous exposure to Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign), with a working familiarity of After EffectsExperience with Microsoft OfficeAbility to work independently and should possess good organizational, computer, written and oral communication skills Notes to Applicant:The Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum is an equal opportunity employer. We respect the varied attributes, characteristics, and perspectives that make each person unique. The museum promotes an environment of respect, communication, and understanding, while actively providing opportunities for all employees of all backgrounds the skills, experience, and information necessary to succeed. The museum does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions), national origin, political affiliation, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, genetic information or characteristics, age, membership in an employee organization, military or veteran status, or other non-merit factor. The Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum does not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics.We are a drug-free workplace and an equal opportunity employer that welcomes all qualified candidates to apply for open positions. The Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum is committed to providing a safe and secure environment for its staff and visitors. All offers of employment are subject to and contingent upon the successful completion of a background check and employment verification, including federally mandated E-Verify processes, as required for position.Due to the high volume of applications received for this position, hiring managers will only contact candidates they are interested in scheduling for an interview. Please refrain from calling to inquire about the status of your application. Please upload a resume and cover letter when applying for the position.Applications are only accepted online on our career page: https://www.countrymusichalloffame.org/careers.

Positions in this class are exempt from the screening and referral requirements of the Iowa Department of Administrative Services - Human Resources Enterprise. Production InternAre you ready to embark on an exciting journey with Iowa PBS, where your passion for creativity meets the power of media?Iowa PBS, Iowa's only statewide television broadcasting network, is searching for two Spring 2027 interns to join our dynamic programming and production division. If you're a college student with a passion for creativity and a desire to make a real impact on the world, our internship offers an experience that will help you achieve just that. About Us: At Iowa PBS, we're not just a network; we're on a mission to educate, inform, enrich, and inspire viewers across the state. We're the folks who bring you those unforgettable local programs, broadcast services, and innovative educational initiatives that shape the future of our communities. Our strength lies in our diverse, talented, and dedicated team members who are at the heart of our mission. When you join us, you're not just an intern; you're a future leader in the making. Role Overview: Iowa PBS is seeking two exceptional Spring 2027 interns within our production division. As a production intern, you'll dive into the world of studio cameras, teleprompters and lighting, gaining hands-on experience in operating professional-grade equipment. You'll work alongside our seasoned videographers, editors, and scenic professionals, developing expertise in the art of content creation, editing, and distribution. The goal of this internship is to empower you to:Master Video Production Techniques: Learn the ins and outs of studio and on-location video production, from camera operation to lighting setups, ensuring you have a solid foundation in the technical aspects of video creation.Editing and Post-Production Skills: Hone your editing skills using industry-standard software, transforming raw footage into polished, engaging content that captivates our audiences.Creative Storytelling: Develop your ability to craft compelling narratives, translating ideas into captivating visual stories that educate and inspire.Team Collaboration: Work closely with a diverse team of professionals, refining your collaboration, communication, and project management skills in a real-world broadcast environment.Problem Solving: Encounter and overcome challenges unique to the world of media production, cultivating a problem-solving mindset that will serve you well in any future endeavor.Audience Engagement: Gain insights into audience preferences and engagement strategies, helping you understand how to connect with viewers on a deeper level.In addition, you can expect to assist with weekly shows like Iowa Press and Market to Market, and get ready for some special projects like covering the girls and boys high school basketball championships, girls and boys high school wrestling championships, college wrestling meets across the state, Iowa's Condition of the State speech, and Iowa PBS's annual Festival pledge drive. By the end of this internship, you'll emerge with a well-rounded skill set, ready to excel in the world of media production and make a meaningful impact in your future career. Why Iowa PBS: Choosing Iowa PBS for your internship isn't just about gaining experience; it's about making a difference. It's about becoming a part of something bigger than yourself. Here, you won't just find a place to work; you'll find a community that values you for your unique ideas and perspectives you bring to the team. We're not just offering an internship; we're offering an enriching experience where every day is an opportunity to grow and shine.Ready to start your adventure with Iowa PBS? Join us as we educate, inform, enrich, and inspire Iowans. If you're passionate about driving positive change and have the dedication to excel in this role, we invite you to become part of our team. Don't miss out on this chance to be a catalyst for positive change and contribute to our vibrant community. Apply now and kickstart your rewarding internship at Iowa PBS today! Iowa PBS is an inclusive workplace and we welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences.Iowa PBS is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. E-Verify and Right to WorkThe State of Iowa participates in E-Verify a federal program that helps employers confirm the employment eligibility of all newly hired employees. Within the required timeframe, new hires will be verified through the E-Verify system to ensure authorization to work in the United States. The State of Iowa also complies with the federal Right to Work laws, which protect employees’ rights to work without being required to join a labor organization. For more information, please visit www.e-verify.gov. Minimum Qualification RequirementsApplicants for positions in this class must be currently enrolled students in a degree program at an accredited educational institution, as determined by the Iowa Department of Administrative Services – Human Resources Enterprise.For additional information, please click on this link to view the job description (Download PDF reader).

The intern will assist with program coordination, administrative tasks, and follow-up communications, while also contributing to research, documentation, and occasional community engagement efforts. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who is highly organized, detail-oriented, and eager to learn. The intern will gain meaningful experience in nonprofit program operations and exposure to national and local journalism leaders through trainings and convenings. Specific ResponsibilitiesProgram coordination: Provide administrative support for Advisory Programs and Communities of Practice including record-keeping, data-entry, tracking deliverables, and assisting with contract drafting and payment form collection for guest speakers. Support program communications, including monitoring community email inboxes and flagging inquires, drafting emails for program participants and conducting follow up.Scheduling & Follow-Ups: Assist with scheduling meetings, setting up Zoom registration links and timely follow-ups with program participants, consultants, and partners.Research & Documentation: Contribute to background research, meeting notetaking, and documentation of program activities and learnings.Community Engagement: Support communications or engagement tasks as needed, including compiling information for newsletters, blog posts, or reports. Support Slack-based engagement and assist the Community Manager with onboarding new community members as needed. Assist with light event support and tracking RSVPs.Professional Development Exposure: Attend and observe monthly Communities of Practice trainings, leadership team meetings, and convenings with newsrooms, consultants, and external partners. QualificationsThe ideal candidate will demonstrate:Strong organizational and administrative skills, with attention to detail.Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Google Suite (Docs, Sheets, Slides).Ability to juggle multiple tasks and follow through reliably.Clear written and verbal communication skills.Interest in journalism, nonprofit programs, or media sustainability (preferred, not required).Undergraduate or graduate student status preferred; candidates with relevant skills and interest are welcome to apply.Employment DetailsThis is a paid internship, offering $18/hourThe position aligns with either your semester or co-op term based on academic calendars.Hybrid work arrangement: in-office on Wednesdays in Philadelphia; other days remote.Approximately 20–35 hours per week, flexible depending on candidate availability.Reports to Head of Advisory Programs, also supports Community/Program ManagerAbout The Lenfest Institute for JournalismThe Lenfest Institute for Journalism is a unique nonprofit organization whose sole mission is to build sustainable business models for local journalism. Guided by the belief that quality local news and information is essential to a healthy, just, vibrant democracy, the Institute supports training, convenings, and grantmaking that strengthen news organizations in Philadelphia and beyond.The Lenfest Institute is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Spring 2027 Museum Education (Paid) Intern at Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
jobs.description: Employer: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum Expires: 10/30/2026 Internship: Museum Education (Paid)For application deadlines and internship dates, please visit: Countrymusichalloffame.org/support/get-involved/internships.Museum Overview: Accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum has been called the “Smithsonian of country music,” celebrated for its broad cultural impact, educational mission, and unrivaled collection of historically important artifacts. Chartered by the state of Tennessee in 1964, the Museum is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, educational organization that documents and interprets the history of country music. The Museum collects objects and archival materials that illustrate the evolving history and traditions of country music and provides diverse learning opportunities through educational programs, publications, and exhibitions.First opened in 1967 on Nashville’s Music Row, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum launched its current downtown location in 2001. In 2014, the Museum unveiled a $100 million expansion that doubled its footprint. The Museum now encompasses 350,000 square feet of exhibition galleries, archival storage, retail stores, and event space. The Museum owns Hatch Show Print, a letterpress print shop opened in 1879, and it operates Historic RCA Studio B, where Dolly Parton, Elvis Presley, and many others recorded. In addition, the Museum offers the Taylor Swift Education Center for students, teachers, and families, and dedicated performance spaces in the CMA Theater and Ford Theater, both of which regularly host nationally recognized live music and cultural events.In 2024, the Museum was awarded the prestigious National Medal of Arts by President Joe Biden. The medal is the highest award given to artists and arts institutions by the United States government. The White House Citation, which accompanied the medal, recognized the Museum’s work, which “preserves history, honors giants of the genre, and inspires future generations to write their own songs about the American story.”Internship Program Overview: The Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum offers paid internships to full-time college students (undergraduate and graduate) that advance the educational goals of the intern and help to promote the Museum’s mission. The Museum’s internship program offers work-based learning opportunities that introduce college students to museum-related careers and other professions found in large cultural organizations. Internships are designed for a maximum commitment of 25 hours per week for 12 weeks with consideration given to individual university requirements. Additional adjustments to the 12-week, 25-hour schedule will be at the discretion of the internship supervisor. Educational programs which operate on a quarterly basis may be accommodated. Motivated students who are seeking hands-on experiences in a team-oriented environment will find excellent opportunities at the Museum.The application process for prospective interns includes the submission of:An online application for the specific internship you are applying for via our internal hiring systemA resumeA one-page cover letter; it is recommended that your cover letter explain how your education and experience will contribute positively to this internship and how this internship relates to your academic pursuits and/or career goals What We Offer Interns:The hourly rate for this position is $15/hr. for students pursuing a bachelor's degree; $18/hr. for students pursuing a master's degree or higherFree 24/7 downtown parking or WeGo bus passComplimentary admission to the Museum for yourselfTwo complimentary Museum admission passes for friends and family useFree guided tour of Hatch Show Print, Historic RCA Studio B, and the Museum’s galleriesDiscounts at Museum stores and restaurants Free or discounted entry to local venues including: National Museum of African American Music, the Opry, Ryman Auditorium, and more! Fun, friendly, and supportive learning environment Field Forward Stipend: Field Forward is a living and relocation stipend, offered to select candidates in addition to the paid internship, that supports students who identify as traditionally underrepresented in cultural arts careers and students with demonstrated financial need. Field Forward’s goals are to encourage diverse student engagement with the Museum and the broader museum field and to promote educational and professional experience and training to students historically underrepresented in museum and other cultural arts professions. Students must submit an additional application and demonstrate financial need (if applicable) to be considered. To learn more, including important deadlines, please visit: Countrymusichalloffame.org/support/get-involved/internships.Departmental Overview: Charged with the mission of educating varied audiences about country music, the Education and Community Engagement department develops programs and resources that illuminate the stories, themes, and music explored in the Museum’s galleries. Serving nearly 100,000 people per year through 1,100 programs, the Education and Community Engagement department supports students of all ages, from school groups and families who engage in hands-on learning activities to general Museum guests who experience performance presentations during their visit. A creative and curious team, staff is composed of traditional and nontraditional educators, including classroom teachers, visual artists, historians, Museum educators, and professional musicians. Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum educators share a passion for country music, popular culture, and lifelong learning and regularly collaborate to develop and implement dynamic educational offerings commensurate with one of the most-visited history museums in America.Museum Education Internship Overview: The Museum Education internship is designed for a commitment of 25 hours per week for a minimum of 12 weeks, flexible within Monday – Friday, 8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. CST. This internship's goal is to engage in a variety of interdisciplinary educational experiences in a museum environment through the School Programs department.School Programs provide dynamic, interdisciplinary learning experiences that support curriculum standards in core subject areas, such STEAM, College and Career Readiness, English Language Arts, Social Studies, Social and Emotional Learning, and fine arts curriculum for grades pre-K–12.The Museum Education intern will receive hands-on training from Museum educators, and they will interact directly with student and teacher audiences. The intern will assist with program delivery and facilitation, support program preparations, facilitate administrative tasks, support evaluation and assessment, attend team meetings, and research and develop resources to support programming.Specific Internship Duties: Assist the School Programs manager in daily activities such as preparing and facilitating student programs in the Museum galleries and classroomsSet specific, personal goals and work with the School Programs manager to achieve themDevelop and practice interdepartmental communication skills and general professionalismPerform administrative tasks as needed RequirementsMinimum Requirements:Currently enrolled, credit-seeking, and/or degree-seeking undergraduate or graduate student Preferred Requirements:Interest in experiential/museum education, music, American history, and youth-focused program development, with course work in a related fieldExperience or course work in education, history, and/or the fine artsKnowledge of country music, or willingness to learnExperience working with children and/or teachingAbility to multitask and solve problemsUpbeat and energetic Conditions of Internship:Be available to work 20-25 hours per week, flexible between Monday – Friday, 8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. CT.Lift 25 lbs. or less Notes to Applicant:The Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum is an equal opportunity employer. We respect the varied attributes, characteristics, and perspectives that make each person unique. The museum promotes an environment of respect, communication, and understanding, while actively providing opportunities for all employees of all backgrounds the skills, experience, and information necessary to succeed. The museum does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions), national origin, political affiliation, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, genetic information or characteristics, age, membership in an employee organization, military or veteran status, or other non-merit factor. The Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum does not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. We are a drug-free workplace and an equal opportunity employer that welcomes all qualified candidates to apply for open positions. The Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum is committed to providing a safe and secure environment for its staff and visitors. All offers of employment are subject to and contingent upon the successful completion of a background check and employment verification, including federally mandated E-Verify processes, as required for position.Due to the high volume of applications received for this position, hiring managers will only contact candidates they are interested in scheduling for an interview. Please refrain from calling to inquire about the status of your application.Please upload a resume and cover letter when applying for the position.Applications are only accepted online on our career page: https://www.countrymusichalloffame.org/careers.

jobs.description: Employer: Apex Park and Recreation District Expires: 10/30/2026 Job Title: Intern – Golf InstructionDepartment: Golf Operations – Indian Tree Golf ClubSupervisor’s Title: Director of Golf and Clubhouse Operations/ Golf Instruction ProfessionalDate Prepared: 9/2026 Job Status: Part-Time, Non-Exempt POSITION PURPOSE: Supports golf instruction, player development, and related golf programming at Indian Tree Golf Club. Works alongside professional golf staff to gain hands-on experience assisting with junior and adult instruction, clinics, camps, individual lessons, player-development programs, and on-course instruction. Provides support for the administrative and operational responsibilities associated with delivering quality golf programming at a public golf facility. This internship is designed to provide meaningful professional development for an individual interested in pursuing a career in golf instruction, PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, or the golf industry. ESSENTIAL DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:Assists golf professionals with individual and group golf instruction for participants of varying ages and skill levels. Supports junior golf camps and clinics, adult programs, beginner programs, and other player-development initiatives. Assists with instruction in putting, chipping, pitching, bunker play, full swing, course management, rules, etiquette, and pace of play. Prepares instructional areas, equipment, training aids, range balls, and other materials prior to programs and lessons. Assists with participant check-in, group organization, instructional stations, and program transitions. Provides basic instructional feedback to participants under the direction of professional golf staff. Assists with on-course instruction on the Par-3 and regulation golf courses. Helps create a positive, encouraging, safe, and welcoming learning environment for golfers of different ages, abilities, skill levels, and backgrounds. Assists with adaptive golf and other programs designed to make golf accessible to a broad range of participants. Assists staff in developing golf clinics, camps, leagues, lesson plans, instructional activities, and other player-development opportunities. Helps evaluate existing programs and identifies opportunities to improve the participant experience. Supports player-development efforts for juniors, beginners, women, seniors, and other developing golfers. Assists with utilizing the driving range, practice facilities, and Par-3 course as player-development resources. Assists with program registration, participation tracking, attendance, participant feedback, and program evaluation. Supports marketing and communication efforts related to golf programs and instructional opportunities. Maintains clean, organized, safe, and professional instructional and practice areas. Consistently represents the Indian Tree Way – Intentional Hospitality, Operational Excellence, and Making It Work when interacting with participants, guests, and coworkers. OTHER DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:Gains exposure to golf shop operations, outside operations, tee-sheet management, pace of play, tournament operations, customer service, and daily golf course operations. Learns policies and procedures related to golf instruction, course access, range operations, safety, and guest service. Gains an understanding of golf program pricing, budgeting, revenue generation, expense management, and other business aspects of operating a public golf facility. Assists with golf shop and outside operations as assigned to gain a broader understanding of golf facility operations. Works with professional golf staff to establish internship learning goals and participates in ongoing coaching and feedback. May be given increasing responsibility for planning and delivering portions of clinics or instructional programs under the supervision of professional golf staff. Develops practical experience in golf instruction and coaching techniques, junior and adult programming, player development, customer service and hospitality, program management and evaluation, and public-sector golf operations. Performs other duties as assigned. SUPERVISORY DUTIES: This position does not have direct supervisory responsibilities. May assist with organizing and directing participants during camps, clinics, lessons, and other instructional activities under the supervision of professional golf staff. JOB QUALIFICATIONS -KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:Working knowledge of golf fundamentals, rules, etiquette, and pace of play. Interest in golf instruction, player development, golf operations, and the golf industry. Ability to effectively communicate with children, adults, guests, and coworkers. Strong customer service and interpersonal skills. Ability to create a positive and welcoming experience for program participants. Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. Ability to follow direction and work within the scope of assigned responsibilities and training. Ability and willingness to learn, accept coaching and feedback, and demonstrate initiative.Ability to maintain a professional appearance and demeanor. Ability to prioritize participant, guest, and employee safety. Ability to organize equipment and instructional materials and assist with multiple activities and participant groups. Ability to work a flexible schedule that may include mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays. Ability to consistently demonstrate the principles of the Indian Tree Way – Intentional Hospitality, Operational Excellence, and Making It Work. EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: Interest in golf instruction, PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, education, coaching, or a related field. Working knowledge of golf fundamentals, rules, and etiquette. Experience or demonstrated ability working effectively with children and adults. CPR/AED/First Aid certification or ability to obtain certification as required.Preferred Qualifications: Currently enrolled in or recently graduated from a PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, education, kinesiology, business, or related program. Previous experience working at a golf course, driving range, golf camp, recreation program, or instructional setting. Previous experience working with children or youth programs. Interest in pursuing PGA membership or a career in golf instruction, player development, or golf operations.WORK ENVIRONMENT: Work is performed in both indoor and outdoor environments at Indian Tree Golf Club, including the golf shop, driving range, practice facilities, Par-3 course, and regulation golf courses. Work may be performed in varying weather and environmental conditions. The position requires regular interaction with children, adults, program participants, guests, and other employees in an active public recreation environment.PHYSICAL ACTIVITIES: Position requires the ability to stand and walk for extended periods, including walking on uneven outdoor terrain and golf course surfaces. Requires frequent bending, reaching, and movement associated with demonstrating golf skills, setting up instructional areas, and assisting with programs. Must be able to handle, move, and set up golf equipment, training aids, range balls, and other instructional materials and equipment. TRAVEL: Limited travel may be required for meetings, training, programs, or other District-related activities. NOTE: This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with the job. May perform other duties as assigned.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Social Media Internship at Huntington Bank
jobs.description: Employer: Huntington Bank Expires: 10/31/2026 Summary: Huntington’s internship programs provide emerging talent with meaningful, hands‑on experience aligned to their area of study. Over the course of the interns’ time at Huntington, they gain exposure to key business functions across all segments of the organization. An intern’s experience should be focused on professional growth, skill development, and practical application of academic learning. Interns participate in a structured series of development opportunities, including interactions with senior leadership and career pathing insights. The experience also includes immersion in Huntington’s award‑winning culture through community involvement and team‑based activities. Internships at Huntington are designed to help students build a strong foundation for future career success while contributing to meaningful business initiatives. Internship Opportunities at Huntington: Huntington offers internship opportunities for students who are currently enrolled in an academic program and seeking practical, hands‑on experience in their field of study. Internships take place during a defined period of time and are available across all business segments. Rising juniors (Winter 2028 or Spring 2029 grads) may participate in Huntington's Foundations Program, an 8-week, regionally focused experience where students partner directly with a manager and team, contribute to meaningful projects, build professional skills, and explore career opportunities across Huntington and the financial services industry. All interns participate in a variety of developmental and professional activities designed to support learning and exposure to the organization. Depending on your school year, program components may include: Experience in day‑to‑day responsibilities related to their assigned team Exposure to broader business functions A structured schedule of professional development sessions Opportunities to engage with members of the Executive Leadership Team Discussions with senior leaders regarding career paths and Huntington’s business areas A team project focused on applying Huntington’s innovation framework to a business‑relevant problem Participation in volunteer activities and internal events aligned with Huntington’s culture Social Media Internship Overview Huntington Bank is seeking creative, curious and collaborative college students to join our Social Media Internship Program.Eligibility note: This internship is open to rising college juniors enrolled during Summer 2027 at one of the Huntington partner schools for this program: University of Michigan, University of Minnesota, West Virginia University, University of Texas, The Ohio State University, University of Mississippi, University of Alabama or Mississippi State University.This internship offers hands-on experience across the full social media content lifecycle within a highly regulated industry. Interns will join Huntington’s editorial content team and work alongside social media, brand, creative, video and production partners to learn how content moves from initial concept through creation, approval, publication and performance evaluation.Each intern will come from one of Huntington’s partner universities and bring their campus perspective into the program. Working remotely from their home communities, with hybrid in-office participation for Columbus-based interns, interns will contribute ideas, insights and content recommendations that help Huntington connect with customers, communities and university audiences across our footprint. As part of the experience, each intern will develop localized content guidance that reflects their campus, student audience and community context. Duties & Responsibilities: Collaborate with fellow interns and mentors to develop social media concepts grounded in audience needs, business goals, cultural moments and emerging platform opportunities.Participate in brainstorming, creative reviews and content planning discussions by presenting concepts, explaining recommendations and contributing constructive feedback.Work with the editorial content team member who creates and delivers Huntington’s advice and guidance newsletter to identify relevant articles and incorporate them into social plans in ways that are useful, timely and audience-aware.Create, edit, optimize and adapt content for a variety of social platforms and formats, including original photo or video content when opportunities arise and repurposed brand, event or partnership assets.Develop a localized social content toolkit, guide or plan for their Huntington partner university, helping the team understand campus culture, student needs, relevant moments and content opportunities, then present their recommendations to the brand team and other relevant Huntington stakeholders at the end of the internship.Support content planning, workflow management, project execution and performance analysis to help improve future social media content. What You'll LearnContent Strategy, Concept Development & Audience Insight: Learn how leading brands identify audience needs, generate ideas and build content strategies that support business objectives, audience engagement, relevant cultural moments and localized opportunities for Huntington partner universities.Content Creation, Storytelling & Editorial-to-Social Integration: Develop skills in social-first storytelling, content production, copywriting, editing, platform adaptation and content optimization, including how advice and guidance articles can be adapted into useful, timely social plans.Creative Pitching, Collaboration & Feedback: Gain experience presenting ideas, explaining creative rationale, communicating recommendations to peers and stakeholders, and refining work through constructive feedback and collaboration.Project Management: Understand how projects move from concept to completion through planning, timelines, approvals and stakeholder coordination.Brand Standards, Compliance & Reputational Risk: Experience how content is created and reviewed within a regulated financial services environment while balancing strong creative ideas with brand standards, business objectives, risk management and reputational considerations.Measurement & Assessment: Learn how social media content is evaluated and how performance insights are used to improve future content strategies. Required SkillsStrong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present ideas clearly.Enthusiasm for social media and a thoughtful understanding of its value, influence, challenges and responsibility as a public-facing communication channel.Creativity, curiosity and willingness to contribute new ideas.Strong organizational skills, attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.Comfort working independently in a remote environment and collaborating effectively with others.Openness to giving, receiving and incorporating constructive feedback. Preferred SkillsExperience creating content for personal, academic, volunteer, student organization, freelance or professional channels, including social media posts, video, photography, graphics, copywriting or other digital storytelling formats.Comfort using creative tools such as CapCut, Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, Final Cut Pro, in-app editing tools within social platforms or similar platforms to edit, design or adapt content.Interest in how social platforms work, including audience engagement, trends, platform best practices and the role social media can play in building connection, trust and action.Experience contributing to group projects, events, campaigns or creative initiatives, including presenting ideas, collaborating with peers and working toward a shared goal. QualificationsRising college junior enrolled during Summer 2027 at one of the Huntington partner schools for this program: University of Michigan, University of Minnesota, West Virginia University, University of Texas, The Ohio State University, University of Mississippi, University of Alabama or Mississippi State University.Pursuing a degree in Marketing, Communications, Journalism, Media, Advertising, Public Relations, Film, Digital Media or a related field. Application ProcessCandidates selected to advance in the interview process will be asked to complete a brief creative exercise demonstrating their understanding of social media audiences, content strategy and storytelling.

jobs.description: Employer: The Autoimmune Fund Expires: 10/31/2026 Graphic Design Intern: The Autoimmune Decade LaunchPart-time, [10 to 15] hrs/week · [Los Angeles area preferred, remote considered] · $20+/hour, depending on experience · Now through January 2027About usThe Autoimmune Fund is a venture fund dedicated exclusively to autoimmune and immune-mediated disease. Our annual report, The Autoimmune Decade, publishes in December 2026 and launches during JPM Healthcare Week in January 2027. We need a designer to make people notice it.What you’ll makeLaunch campaign. A LinkedIn-first social series: teasers, finding cards, carousels, and event graphics for JPM week.Fund infographics. Turn our findings into visuals people share, not charts for slides.Science visuals. Clear, accurate, original images that explain immunology to investors and patients.How you’ll workThe founder sets the story for each piece. You find the idea and design it. Our creative director reviews and finishes it. You work inside a brand system, and every number comes from our verified research.You haveA portfolio that shows original ideas, not just clean execution. Campaign, editorial, illustration, or motion work all count.Fluency in Figma and/or Adobe IllustratorThe ability to take feedback and revise fastPlus: a biology, health, or science background, or experience in medical or scientific illustrationHow to applySend your portfolio, resume, and response to the prompt below to bonnie@autoimmune.fund with the subject line “Design Intern: [Your Name].” Applications without the prompt will not be reviewed.The Prompt The Autoimmune Decade puts a price on autoimmune disease. It launches in January 2027. Most people scroll past the word “autoimmune.” Your job is to make them stop.1. Find the idea.Sketch three different campaign directions for the launch. Rough is fine: a line, a visual, a thumbnail each. Pick one and tell us in three sentences why it wins.2. Make the hero post.Using your chosen direction, design one finished LinkedIn post (1080 x 1350) built around one of these two facts:From 2014 to 2025, of $40.0 billion in venture capital invested in autoimmune and immune-mediated disease, 94% went to drug therapeutics. Everything else (diagnosis, prediction, devices, care) shared 6%.Women with lupus wait about twice as long as men to be diagnosed: a median of 29.6 months, compared with 14.1 months.3. Explain the science your way.In autoimmune disease, the immune system mistakes the body’s own tissue for a threat. Invent a visual metaphor for that. Show two or three rough options, then finish the one you’d carry forward. In two sentences, tell us where your metaphor breaks down. Every metaphor does somewhere; we want to know you can see it.RulesOriginal work only. No AI-generated imagery, no stock or downloaded icons.Start from our palette: dark green #213E3B, teal #42AA8B, light teal #97D5C2, off-white #F8F8F8. Push it if your idea needs it, and tell us why.Bold idea, disciplined execution. US spelling, no em dashes.Send everything as one PDF. We care more about your thinking than your polish, so include your sketches.

jobs.title: Media Specialist at Camp Bear Creek
jobs.description: Employer: Camp Bear Creek Expires: 11/01/2026 Media Specialist – Summer StaffLocation: Camp Bear Creek – Eastern IowaWebsite: https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/Dates: May 23-July 24, 2027Camp Bear Creek is a Christian summer camp in Eastern Iowa serving kids from kindergarten through 12th grade. We’re looking for passionate, fun, dedicated people who want to spend a summer making a real difference — in the lives of campers and in their own.Come work as a Media Specialist at Camp Bear Creek. We are seeking a talented individual who is ready to put their skills into practice. The Media Specialist for the summer gains a lot of experience in, well, all things media. However, you also have the chance to do a lot more than that. You'll be immersed in the summer camp environment, interacting with children and youth in a Christian setting, learning how to capture their stories and how to share the mission of the camp, the joy of the moment, and the magic of summer in something as simple as a photograph or as complex as a ten minute video.The Media Specialist is responsible for camp photography and videography. You'll be out there with the camera, whether it's a DSLR or the GoPro, capturing that kid's giant smile as they go flying down the slip 'n slide or the moment they make it to the top of the rock wall or their splash landing at the bottom of the mud slide. The Media Specialist maintains the daily summer camp blog, which parents depend on as one of their only sources of communication with their child while they're away for six days at camp. They want to know what it feels like to be at camp even when they can't be there themselves, and the best Media Specialist will be able to help them do that. The Media Specialist updates the camp social media accounts, engaging a diverse community of all ages and experiences that spans back over a 65 year history. The Media Specialist designs a weekly summary video, compiling everything that they have captured during the week and uniquely putting it all together into an 8-10 minute video that parents and campers will not only watch over and over, but they'll want to show others because it so perfectly captures what camp was like.If you think you're ready for a summer like this and to be the Media Specialist, please complete the application through the camp’s website at https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/ You'll walk away from the summer with a bigger portfolio, college credit, and a wealth of experience. Plus, you can't discount the chance to have some fun at camp, either!
